items.title: Kalshi ends volume rewards program on October 13
items.content_text: - **Kalshi ends volume rewards program on October 13** — KalshiEX notified the CFTC on September 28 that it is terminating its Volume Incentive Program, effective no earlier than October 13, 2026, far ahead of its original October 2027 end date. The program paid eligible traders a share of fixed per-market rewards based on qualifying volume to boost liquidity; market makers, affiliates, and certain customers were excluded, and no replacement program was announced. ([Crypto Economy](https://crypto-economy.com/kalshi-ends-volume-rewards-program/))

items.title: Polymarket tests Protocol V2 ahead of November 2 cutover for new markets
items.content_text: - **Polymarket tests Protocol V2 ahead of November 2 cutover for new markets** — Polymarket is running production canary markets on a rebuilt smart-contract system through October 30, with a tentative switch to Protocol V2 for all newly created markets on November 2. The upgrade replaces the 2019 Gnosis-based framework with a single ERC-1155 positions contract, pUSD as collateral, and a modular oracle setup, backed by a $5 million bug bounty. items.content_text: - **CFTC moves to define prediction-market event contracts as swaps, excludes casino-style gambling** — The CFTC on October 9 issued an interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling from the definition of a swap and a companion proposal to explicitly classify event contracts tied to sports, politics, culture and weather as swaps. Chairman Selig says the contracts are commodity derivatives within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction; the move comes as the state-federal fight heads toward the Supreme Court. items.content_text: - **Kalshi seeks full 6th Circuit review of states' regulation win** — Kalshi asked the full Sixth Circuit to review a three-judge panel ruling that Ohio and Tennessee can regulate it as unlicensed online sports gambling, arguing the panel erred and pointing to the CFTC's same-day proposals defining sports and other event contracts as federal swaps. items.content_text: - **39 states, NFL, Dodd and Gensler file Supreme Court amicus briefs as CFTC moves to classify prediction contracts as swaps** — Last week 39 states plus D.C., 145 tribal nations, the NFL, former Senator Chris Dodd and former CFTC chair Gary Gensler filed amicus briefs urging the Supreme Court to take up whether sports prediction contracts qualify as swaps, with most siding with state authority. On Friday the CFTC answered with an interim final rule and a new proposal explicitly classifying sports, political and other event contracts as federal swaps; Kalshi's deadline to respond was extended to November 9. ([KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/39-states-and-cftc-clash-over-regulation-of-sports-prediction-markets))

items.content_text: - **Reuters/Ipsos poll finds bipartisan opposition to election prediction markets** — A Reuters/Ipsos poll of 4,506 U.S. adults found bipartisan opposition to election betting on prediction markets, with 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans opposed.
